source.text: Πρὸ δὲ τῆς ἑορτῆς τοῦ πάσχα εἰδὼς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἦλθεν αὐτοῦ ἡ ὥρα ἵνα μεταβῇ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου τούτου πρὸς τὸν πατέρα ἀγαπήσας τοὺς ἰδίους τοὺς ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ εἰς τέλος ἠγάπησεν αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: Before now the feast of the Passover, knowing the Jesus that came his the hour that he should pass out of the world this to the Father, having loved the own the [ones] in the world, to [the] end he loved them.

en.L: Now before the feast of the Passover, Jesus, knowing that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hour had come that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} should pass out of this world to the Father, having loved {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own who [were] in the world, loved them to the end.
en.B: It was just before the Passover festival. Jesus knew that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hour had come, the hour for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to pass from this world to the Father. He had loved {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own who were in the world, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loved them to the end.
en.R: It was just before the Passover festival. Jesus knew that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hour had come, the time for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to leave this world and go to the Father. He had always loved the people in the world who belonged to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loved them to the very end, with a love that held nothing back.

es.L: Antes de la fiesta de la Pascua, sabiendo Jesús que había llegado su hora de pasar de este mundo al Padre, habiendo amado a los suyos que [estaban] en el mundo, los amó hasta el fin.
es.B: Era justo antes de la fiesta de la Pascua. Jesús sabía que había llegado su hora, la hora de pasar de este mundo al Padre. Había amado a los suyos que estaban en el mundo, y los amó hasta el fin.
es.R: Era justo antes de la fiesta de la Pascua. Jesús sabía que había llegado su hora, el momento de dejar este mundo e ir al Padre. Siempre había amado a los que eran suyos en el mundo, y ahora los amó hasta el final, con un amor que no se guardó nada.

sw.L: Basi kabla ya sikukuu ya Pasaka, Yesu, akijua kwamba saa {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ilikuwa imefika ya kutoka katika ulimwengu huu kwenda kwa Baba, akiwa amewapenda walio {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} waliokuwa ulimwenguni, aliwapenda mpaka mwisho.
sw.B: Ilikuwa kabla kidogo ya sikukuu ya Pasaka. Yesu alijua kwamba saa {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ilikuwa imefika, saa ya kutoka katika ulimwengu huu kwenda kwa Baba. Alikuwa amewapenda walio {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} waliokuwa ulimwenguni, naye aliwapenda mpaka mwisho.
sw.R: Ilikuwa kabla kidogo ya sikukuu ya Pasaka. Yesu alijua kwamba saa {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ilikuwa imefika, wakati wa kuuacha ulimwengu huu na kwenda kwa Baba. Siku zote alikuwa amewapenda watu wa ulimwenguni waliokuwa {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, na sasa aliwapenda mpaka mwisho kabisa, kwa upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wote.

vi.L: Trước kỳ Lễ Vượt Qua, Đức Giê-xu biết rằng giờ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đến để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rời khỏi thế gian này mà về với Cha, và đã yêu thương những người thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở trong thế gian, thì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} yêu thương họ đến cùng.
vi.B: Lúc ấy là ngay trước Lễ Vượt Qua. Đức Giê-xu biết giờ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đến, giờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rời thế gian này để về với Cha. Ngài đã yêu thương những người thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong thế gian, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} yêu thương họ đến cùng.
vi.R: Lúc ấy là ngay trước Lễ Vượt Qua. Đức Giê-xu biết giờ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đến, đó là lúc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rời thế gian này để về với Cha. Ngài luôn yêu thương những người trong thế gian thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} yêu thương họ đến tận cùng, một tình yêu không giữ lại điều gì.

decisions.choice: to the end: both to the end of his life and to the uttermost, completely
alternatives: to the end (of his life) only
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "to the end" in time or "completely, to the limit". Here both fit, and John seems to mean both: Jesus loved his own up to the end of his life, and he loved them with a love that went all the way. The noun is related to the verb Jesus speaks from the cross, "It is finished" (19:30). A footnote gives the second sense.

decisions.choice: his hour: the appointed time of his death and return to the Father, now come
decisions.reason: Until now the hour "had not yet come" (2:4; 7:30; 8:20). In 12:23 Jesus says that it has come. The narrator now says so too, and adds what the hour is: the time for Jesus to pass from this world to the Father, through his death.

decisions.choice: pass out of this world to the Father: Jesus's death seen as a going from one place to another
decisions.reason: The verb means to move or pass from one place to another, as in 5:24 ("has passed from death to life"). Jesus's death is his return to the Father from whom he came (16:28). "This world" here is the world in which people live, which Jesus is leaving and in which his own remain (17:11).

decisions.choice: his own: those who belong to Jesus, his disciples
decisions.reason: In 1:11 "his own" were his own people, who did not receive him. Here "his own" are those who did: the sheep who know his voice (10:3-4, 14), the people the Father has given him (17:6). They are "in the world" and will stay there when he goes (17:11). The love he had shown them all along now reaches its fullest point.

decisions.choice: before the Passover: the supper takes place on the evening before the feast
decisions.reason: In John the Jewish leaders have not yet eaten the Passover meal when Jesus is handed to Pilate (18:28), and he is condemned on the day of preparation for the Passover (19:14). The meal in this chapter is therefore before the Passover. John does not call it a Passover meal, as the other Gospels do (Mark 14:12-16).

decisions.choice: hour, at every level
decisions.reason: As in 12:23-27, the word stays "hour" at every level so that the thread of Jesus's hour can be followed through the Gospel (meaning decision m2). Readable adds "the time for him" to explain it.

decisions.choice: three sentences (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek is one sentence held together by two participles ("knowing", "having loved"). Balanced and Readable state the time, then what Jesus knew, then his love, each in its own sentence.

decisions.choice: had always loved; to the very end, with a love that held nothing back
decisions.reason: Readable gives both senses of the phrase (meaning decision m1), and "always" shows that "having loved" looks back over his whole time with them.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}, {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: Pronouns for Jesus take the deity_pronoun setting; "He" at the start of a sentence is capitalized either way.

decisions.choice: hora, at every level
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for the appointed hour (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: hasta el fin (L, B); hasta el final, con un amor que no se guardó nada (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish "hasta el fin" keeps both senses, to the end of his life and to the uttermost (meaning decision m1); Readable spells out the second, as in English.

decisions.choice: mpaka mwisho (L, B); mpaka mwisho kabisa, kwa upendo wake wote (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning note gives both senses: to the end of his life and to the uttermost. "Mpaka mwisho" holds both, as the English "to the end" does; "kikamilifu" (fully) would keep only the second. Readable spells out the second sense, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "đến cùng" (L, B); "đến tận cùng" (R)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "đến cùng" means both "to the end" and "to the utmost", so it keeps the double sense the meaning decision describes; "cho đến cuối cùng" would keep only the time.

source.text: καὶ δείπνου γινομένου, τοῦ διαβόλου ἤδη βεβληκότος εἰς τὴν καρδίαν ἵνα παραδοῖ αὐτὸν Ἰούδας Σίμωνος Ἰσκαριώτου, εἰδὼς ὅτι πάντα ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ ὁ πατὴρ εἰς τὰς χεῖρας, καὶ ὅτι ἀπὸ θεοῦ ἐξῆλθεν καὶ πρὸς τὸν θεὸν ὑπάγει, ἐγείρεται ἐκ τοῦ δείπνου καὶ τίθησιν τὰ ἱμάτια καὶ λαβὼν λέντιον διέζωσεν ἑαυτόν·

records.literal_gloss: And supper taking place, the devil already having put into the heart that should betray him Judas [son] of Simon Iscariot, \v 3 knowing that all things gave to him the Father into the hands, and that from God he came out and to the God he is going away, \v 4 he rises from the supper and lays the garments, and having taken a towel he girded himself;

en.L: And while supper was taking place, the devil having already put into the heart that Judas [son] of Simon Iscariot should hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over, \v 3 [Jesus], knowing that the Father had given all things into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands, and that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had come out from God and was going away to God, \v 4 rises from the supper and lays aside the garments, and taking a towel, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} tied [it] around {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.
en.B: Supper was under way, and the devil had already put the thought of betraying Jesus into the heart of Judas, son of Simon Iscariot. \v 3 Jesus knew that the Father had put everything into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands. He knew too that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had come out from God and was on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way back to God. \v 4 He got up from the meal, put aside {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} outer garments, took a towel and tied it around {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} waist.
en.R: Jesus and the disciples were eating the evening meal. Even before this, the devil had put into the heart of Judas the idea of betraying Jesus. Judas was the son of Simon Iscariot. \v 3 Jesus knew that the Father had given {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} power over everything. He also knew that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came from God and would soon go back to God. \v 4 He got up from the meal and took off {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} outer clothes. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took a towel and tied it around {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} waist.

es.L: Y mientras se celebraba la cena, habiendo ya puesto el diablo en el corazón que Judas, [hijo] de Simón Iscariote, lo entregara, \v 3 [Jesús], sabiendo que el Padre le había dado todas las cosas en las manos, y que había salido de Dios y a Dios volvía, \v 4 se levanta de la cena y pone a un lado el manto, y tomando una toalla, se la ciñó.
es.B: La cena estaba en marcha, y el diablo ya había puesto en el corazón de Judas, hijo de Simón Iscariote, la idea de traicionar a Jesús. \v 3 Jesús sabía que el Padre había puesto todo en sus manos. Sabía también que había salido de Dios y que volvía a Dios. \v 4 Se levantó de la cena, se quitó el manto, tomó una toalla y se la ató a la cintura.
es.R: Jesús y los discípulos estaban cenando. Ya antes de esto, el diablo había puesto en el corazón de Judas la idea de traicionar a Jesús. Judas era hijo de Simón Iscariote. \v 3 Jesús sabía que el Padre le había dado poder sobre todas las cosas. También sabía que había venido de Dios y que pronto volvería a Dios. \v 4 Se levantó de la mesa y se quitó la ropa de encima. Luego tomó una toalla y se la ató a la cintura.

sw.L: Na chakula cha jioni kilipokuwa kikiendelea, Ibilisi akiwa amekwisha kutia moyoni kwamba Yuda [mwana] wa Simoni Iskariote amtoe, \v 3 [Yesu], akijua kwamba Baba amempa vitu vyote mikononi {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}, na kwamba alitoka kwa Mungu na anakwenda kwa Mungu, \v 4 anaondoka chakulani na kuweka kando mavazi, na akitwaa kitambaa, akajifunga kiunoni.
sw.B: Chakula cha jioni kilikuwa kikiendelea, na Ibilisi alikuwa amekwisha kutia moyoni mwa Yuda, mwana wa Simoni Iskariote, wazo la kumsaliti Yesu. \v 3 Yesu alijua kwamba Baba alikuwa ameweka kila kitu mikononi {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}. Alijua pia kwamba alikuwa ametoka kwa Mungu na kwamba alikuwa njiani kurudi kwa Mungu. \v 4 Akainuka kutoka chakulani, akavua mavazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ya nje, akachukua kitambaa na kukifunga kiunoni {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}.
sw.R: Yesu na wanafunzi walikuwa wakila chakula cha jioni. Hata kabla ya hapo, Ibilisi alikuwa ametia moyoni mwa Yuda wazo la kumsaliti Yesu. Yuda alikuwa mwana wa Simoni Iskariote. \v 3 Yesu alijua kwamba Baba alikuwa amempa mamlaka juu ya kila kitu. Alijua pia kwamba alitoka kwa Mungu na kwamba hivi karibuni angerudi kwa Mungu. \v 4 Akainuka kutoka chakulani, akavua nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} za nje. Kisha akachukua kitambaa, akakifunga kiunoni {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}.

vi.L: Và trong khi bữa ăn tối đang diễn ra, ma quỷ đã đặt vào lòng Giu-đa, con của Si-môn Ích-ca-ri-ốt, [ý định] nộp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \v 3 [Đức Giê-xu] biết rằng Cha đã giao mọi sự vào tay {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã từ Đức Chúa Trời mà đến và đang trở về với Đức Chúa Trời, \v 4 thì đứng dậy khỏi bữa ăn, cởi áo ngoài ra, và lấy một cái khăn thắt quanh mình.
vi.B: Bữa ăn tối đang diễn ra, và ma quỷ đã đặt vào lòng Giu-đa, con của Si-môn Ích-ca-ri-ốt, ý định phản bội Đức Giê-xu. \v 3 Đức Giê-xu biết rằng Cha đã giao mọi sự vào tay {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Ngài cũng biết rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã từ Đức Chúa Trời mà đến và đang trở về với Đức Chúa Trời. \v 4 Ngài đứng dậy khỏi bữa ăn, cởi áo ngoài ra, lấy một cái khăn và quấn ngang lưng.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu và các môn đồ đang ăn bữa tối. Trước đó, ma quỷ đã đặt vào lòng Giu-đa ý định phản bội Đức Giê-xu. Giu-đa là con của Si-môn Ích-ca-ri-ốt. \v 3 Đức Giê-xu biết rằng Cha đã ban cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} quyền trên mọi sự. Ngài cũng biết rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã từ Đức Chúa Trời mà đến và sắp trở về với Đức Chúa Trời. \v 4 Ngài đứng dậy khỏi bữa ăn và cởi áo ngoài ra. Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lấy một cái khăn quấn ngang lưng.

decisions.choice: while supper was taking place (SBLGNT)
alternatives: after supper, or when supper had begun (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Codex Vaticanus, the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus and some other early manuscripts have the present tense, "while supper was taking place". Many other manuscripts, followed by the KJV ("supper being ended"), have the aorist, which can mean "when supper was over". The washing happens during the meal, since Jesus gets up from it and returns to it (13:12) and the meal goes on afterward (13:26). A footnote gives the other reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the devil had put into the heart of Judas the purpose of betraying Jesus
alternatives: the devil had already decided in his own heart that Judas would betray him
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "put into the heart", without saying whose heart, and then names Judas as the one who would betray. The most natural reading is that the devil put the thought into Judas's heart; 13:27 says that Satan entered him. Many later manuscripts make this explicit by putting Judas's name in the form "of Judas", joined to "the heart". The words could also mean that the devil had made up his own mind that Judas would betray Jesus, since "to put into the heart" can mean "to decide". A footnote gives the other reading.

decisions.choice: the devil: the enemy of God, already at work behind the betrayal
decisions.reason: John has called the devil a murderer and a liar (8:44) and called Judas "a devil" for doing his work (6:70). The word "already" shows that the betrayal is under way before Jesus begins to wash feet. Jesus serves even the one who will hand him over.

decisions.choice: hand him over: betray him; Judas son of Simon Iscariot, as in 6:71
decisions.reason: The verb means to hand over, and for Judas it means betrayal (6:64, 71). As in 6:71, the name Iscariot agrees in form with Simon, so it describes the father as well as the son.

decisions.choice: given all things into his hands: given him full authority over everything
decisions.reason: To give something into someone's hands is to put it under their power. John has said the same in 3:35 ("The Father loves the Son and has given all things into his hand"). Jesus goes to his death knowing that nothing is outside his control (10:18).

decisions.choice: knowing who he is, he rises to do a slave's task
decisions.reason: The long sentence sets Jesus's full knowledge of his authority, his origin and his goal right beside the plain actions that follow. He does not wash feet in spite of knowing who he is, nor because he forgets it; he does it knowing it. The same pattern of the Lord serving is drawn out in 13:13-16.

decisions.choice: the garments: his outer clothing, the cloak worn over the tunic
decisions.reason: The plural word means outer clothing, as in 19:23, where it is distinguished from the tunic. Jesus is left in the tunic, dressed like a slave for work.

decisions.choice: lays aside ... taking: perhaps an echo of laying down and taking up his life
alternatives: ordinary words for undressing and dressing, with no further meaning
decisions.reason: The verb "lays aside" is the one Jesus uses for laying down his life (10:11, 15, 17-18), and in 13:12 he "took" his garments again, the verb used for taking his life up again (10:17-18). The washing may picture his death. John does not say so, and both verbs are common, so this is uncertain.

decisions.choice: Historic present: rises, lays aside (L); got up, laid aside (B, R)
decisions.reason: John often tells past events in the present tense to make them vivid ("he rises", "he lays aside", "he pours", "he comes", "he says"). Literal keeps the present throughout this passage so that readers see the Greek form; Balanced and Readable use the past, which is the normal tense for telling a story in English. This decision applies to every historic present in 13:1-11.

decisions.choice: several sentences; laid aside (L), put aside (B), took off (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek is one long sentence: a setting, two things Jesus knew, then four actions. Balanced and Readable give each part its own sentence and name Jesus again so that the subject is clear.

decisions.choice: hand over (L); betray (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 6:64 and 6:71 (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: [Jesus] (L); the thought of, the heart of Judas (B); Jesus and the disciples were eating; the idea of (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek does not name Jesus as the subject of verses 3-4, since he was named in verse 1, so Literal supplies him in brackets. Balanced and Readable follow the reading in meaning decision m2 and say whose heart it was. Readable says who was eating.

decisions.choice: had given him power over everything
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom "into his hands" (meaning decision m5).

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal; pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John: Literal keeps John's present ("dice", "ven"); Balanced and Readable use the pretérito. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: entregara (L); traicionar (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English and at 6:71 (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: pone a un lado el manto
decisions.reason: Literal uses "poner", the verb of 10:11 and 10:17 ("pone su vida"), so the possible echo of laying down his life can be seen (meaning decision m8).

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anaondoka, anamimina in verse 5, anakuja in verse 6); past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As in the earlier chapters, for the whole of chapter 13.

decisions.choice: amtoe (L); kumsaliti (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal keeps the plain verb "to hand over" (kumtoa), as at 12:4; Balanced and Readable say what the handing over is, a betrayal. The same in verses 11 and 21.

decisions.choice: "[ý định]" (L)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese cannot leave "put into the heart" without an object; the bracket supplies "the purpose" the meaning decision names.

decisions.choice: "thắt quanh mình" (L); "quấn ngang lưng" (B, R), with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The reflexive "mình" stands for the English "himself/Himself" and needs no setting.

source.text: εἶτα βάλλει ὕδωρ εἰς τὸν νιπτῆρα, καὶ ἤρξατο νίπτειν τοὺς πόδας τῶν μαθητῶν καὶ ἐκμάσσειν τῷ λεντίῳ ᾧ ἦν διεζωσμένος.

records.literal_gloss: Then he puts water into the basin, and began to wash the feet of the disciples and to wipe with the towel with which he was girded.

en.L: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} pours water into the basin, and began to wash the feet of the disciples and to wipe [them] with the towel which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had tied on.
en.B: Next {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} poured water into the basin and began washing the disciples' feet, drying them with the towel {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had tied around {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} poured water into a large bowl. He began to wash the feet of the disciples and to dry them with the towel around {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} waist.

es.L: Luego echa agua en la palangana, y comenzó a lavar los pies de los discípulos y a secar[los] con la toalla con que estaba ceñido.
es.B: Después echó agua en la palangana y comenzó a lavar los pies de los discípulos, secándoselos con la toalla que se había atado a la cintura.
es.R: Luego echó agua en una vasija grande. Comenzó a lavarles los pies a los discípulos y a secárselos con la toalla que tenía atada a la cintura.

sw.L: Kisha anamimina maji katika bakuli, akaanza kuiosha miguu ya wanafunzi na kuipangusa kwa kile kitambaa alichokuwa amejifunga.
sw.B: Kisha akamimina maji katika bakuli, akaanza kuwaosha wanafunzi miguu, akiipangusa kwa kitambaa alichokuwa amejifunga kiunoni.
sw.R: Kisha akamimina maji katika beseni kubwa. Akaanza kuwaosha wanafunzi miguu na kuipangusa kwa kitambaa kilichokuwa kiunoni {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}.

vi.L: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đổ nước vào chậu, và bắt đầu rửa chân các môn đồ và lau [chân họ] bằng cái khăn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã thắt quanh mình.
vi.B: Kế đó, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đổ nước vào chậu và bắt đầu rửa chân cho các môn đồ, rồi lau khô bằng chiếc khăn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã quấn quanh mình.
vi.R: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đổ nước vào một cái chậu lớn. Ngài bắt đầu rửa chân cho các môn đồ và lau khô bằng chiếc khăn quấn ngang lưng.

decisions.choice: washing feet: a task for a slave or the lowest member of a household
decisions.reason: People walked dusty roads in sandals, so a host gave guests water to wash their feet (Genesis 18:4; Luke 7:44). The washing itself was usually done by a slave; Abigail offers to wash the feet of David's servants as the lowest of slaves (1 Samuel 25:41). A teacher washing his disciples' feet reverses the usual order (13:13-16).

decisions.choice: began to wash: the one with all authority (13:3) does the slave's work
decisions.reason: John places this act directly after saying that the Father had given all things into Jesus's hands. The contrast is the point: Jesus uses his authority to serve. "Began" also prepares for Peter's interruption in verse 6.

decisions.choice: wipe: perhaps an echo of Mary wiping Jesus's feet (12:3)
decisions.reason: The verb "to wipe" is the one used of Mary, who anointed Jesus's feet and wiped them with her hair (12:3; 11:2). What Mary did for Jesus, Jesus now does for his disciples. The link is likely but not certain, since the verb is the natural one for drying.

decisions.choice: basin (L, B); large bowl (R); wipe (L); dry (B, R)
decisions.reason: The basin is a washing bowl. Balanced and Readable say "dry", which is what wiping wet feet with a towel does. Literal keeps "wipe" to show the link with 12:3 (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: pours ... began (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps John's change from present to past (historic present; see 13:2-4, decision r-en-1).

decisions.choice: palangana (L, B); vasija grande (R); secar
decisions.reason: As in English.

vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu đến chỗ Si-môn Phi-e-rơ.

decisions.choice: so he comes: the story moves on to Peter; John does not say whether Peter was first
alternatives: Peter came after some of the others
decisions.reason: The word "so" carries the story forward. John does not say how many disciples Jesus had washed before he came to Peter, and the text does not settle it.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus, since the sentence is short and stands at the start of a new scene.

decisions.choice: Jesús
decisions.reason: As in English.

decisions.choice: you ... my: the two pronouns side by side show how wrong it seems to Peter
decisions.reason: The pronoun "you" is written out for emphasis and placed next to "my": you, my Lord, wash my feet? The present tense can mean "are you about to", since Jesus has come to Peter but has not yet begun.

decisions.choice: Lord: the address of a disciple to his master
decisions.reason: Peter is one of the Twelve and speaks to Jesus as his Lord (6:68). In 13:13 Jesus himself says that they rightly call him Teacher and Lord.

decisions.choice: Peter; are you going to (B); are you really going to (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker and use "going to" for an act that is about to happen (meaning decision m1). Readable adds "really" to show Peter's surprise.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}
decisions.reason: Pronouns for Jesus, including "you" when Peter speaks to him, take the deity_pronoun setting. "My" here is Peter's and takes none.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me
decisions.reason: Spanish keeps the stressed "tú" next to "me" at every level, as the Greek sets the two pronouns side by side (meaning decision m1); the stressed pronoun takes the setting.

decisions.choice: Señor
decisions.reason: A disciple's address to his master (meaning decision m2); "Señor" at every level, as elsewhere in John.

decisions.choice: Bwana, capitalised
decisions.reason: Here a disciple addresses his master, so "Bwana" (Lord) is capitalised, as in the English; the polite "bwana" (sir) of John 4-6 and 12:21 is placed inside the sentence and kept lowercase. The same in verses 9, 25, 36 and 37.

decisions.choice: "Thưa Chúa, Chúa ... con" for Peter speaking to Jesus, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: A disciple says "Chúa" for kyrie (docs/john-terms.md) and Vietnamese then uses the same noun as "you", with "con" for himself; nouns of address are always capitalised and take no setting.

alignments.target_span: you will come to know it

decisions.choice: I ... you: both pronouns are emphatic, setting what Jesus does against what Peter can grasp
decisions.reason: The Greek writes out both "I" and "you". Jesus answers Peter's emphatic "you" (13:6): what I am doing is beyond what you, as yet, understand.

decisions.choice: know ... will know: Peter does not grasp it now, but will come to understand
decisions.reason: John uses two different verbs for knowing here; together they say that Peter lacks understanding now and will gain it.

decisions.choice: after these things: after Jesus's death and resurrection
alternatives: in a few moments, when Jesus explains it (13:12-17)
decisions.reason: John often says that the disciples understood only later what Jesus did and said, when he was raised and glorified (2:22; 12:16), and the Spirit would remind them (14:26). Jesus explains part of the act at once (13:12-17), but its full meaning comes after the cross.

decisions.choice: know ... come to know (B); understand (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced shows the move from not knowing to coming to know; Readable says "understand", the plain sense of both verbs here (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Lo que yo hago, tú no lo sabes
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep both emphatic pronouns (meaning decision m1). "Yo" is not under the setting.

decisions.choice: "con" for Jesus addressing Peter
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to a disciple as a teacher to one in his care, matching "các con" for the group.

decisions.choice: the strongest possible refusal: never, not ever
decisions.reason: Two negatives together make the strongest denial Greek has, and "to the age" adds "ever". Peter is not asking; he refuses outright.

decisions.choice: Peter refuses out of respect for his Lord
decisions.reason: To Peter it is unthinkable that his Lord should do a slave's task for him (meaning decision m1 of 13:6). His refusal comes from honor for Jesus, but it also resists what Jesus has chosen to do, as Peter will later resist Jesus's arrest (18:10-11).

decisions.choice: never going to ... not ever (B); No! I will never let you (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced repeats the negative to carry the force of the Greek. Readable turns it into Peter's refusal to allow it, which is what the strong negative means in the mouth of the one being served.

decisions.choice: jamás (L); nunca, jamás (B); ¡No! ¡Nunca ...! (R)
decisions.reason: The strongest refusal Spanish has (meaning decision m1). The B "Tú" opens the sentence and is written plain.

vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đáp lời ông: "Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không rửa cho con, con sẽ không có phần với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu đáp lời ông: "Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không rửa cho con, con không thể thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."

decisions.choice: a share with me: a place among those who belong to Jesus and share in what is his
alternatives: a share in the task of serving others
decisions.reason: The word means a part or share, as in an inheritance (Luke 15:12) or a portion in the land (the Levites had "no part or inheritance", Deuteronomy 12:12). To have a share "with" Jesus is to belong to him and share his life and his place with the Father (14:3; 17:24). Without what Jesus is doing, Peter cannot be one of his own (13:1).

decisions.choice: wash you: the washing points beyond the feet to the cleansing Jesus gives
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say "your feet" but "you". The washing stands for what Jesus does for his own through his death, which Peter does not yet understand (13:7). Peter must receive it, not refuse it.

decisions.choice: part (L); can have no share (B); cannot belong to (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "share", the word for a portion that belongs to someone; "can" makes clear that the second half follows from the first. Readable says what having a share with Jesus means (meaning decision m1); this narrows a word with a wider sense.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of himself, so "me" takes the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: no podrás tener parte conmigo (B); no podrás ser de los míos (R)
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: sehemu (L); fungu (B); kuwa wangu (R)
decisions.reason: "Fungu" is a share or portion, the sense in the meaning note: a place among those who belong to Jesus. Readable says it straight out, "you cannot be mine". "Urithi" (inheritance) would add an idea the word does not carry here.

decisions.choice: "wash" is understood: not only my feet, but my hands and head too
decisions.reason: Peter leaves out the verb; it is plain from what Jesus has just said.

decisions.choice: Peter swings from refusal to excess, still not understanding
decisions.reason: If being washed means having a share with Jesus, Peter wants as much of it as he can have. His eagerness is real, but he still thinks of the washing as a matter of how much water, which Jesus corrects in verse 10.

decisions.choice: Lord: a disciple's address to Jesus, as in 13:6
decisions.reason: Peter again calls Jesus Lord, as a disciple speaking to his master (13:6, 13).

decisions.choice: Then (B, R); wash (R)
decisions.reason: "Then" shows that Peter is answering what Jesus has just said. Readable supplies the verb Peter leaves out (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Entonces (B, R); lávame (R)
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m1).

en.R: Jesus answered, "A person who has taken a bath is clean all over. Only the feet need washing. You are clean too, but not all of you."

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu phán với ông: "Người đã tắm rồi thì không cần gì ngoài việc rửa chân, nhưng được sạch cả; và các con đã sạch, nhưng không phải tất cả [các con]."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu phán với ông: "Ai đã tắm rồi thì chỉ cần rửa chân, vì cả người đã sạch. Các con cũng sạch, nhưng không phải tất cả."

decisions.choice: except the feet (SBLGNT)
alternatives: The one who has bathed has no need to wash, but is clean all over (Codex Sinaiticus and some Latin witnesses)
decisions.reason: Codex Sinaiticus and some Latin witnesses lack "except the feet". Without the words, Jesus says: "The one who has bathed has no need to wash, but is clean all over." Then the bath itself is the cleansing Jesus gives, and the foot-washing is that bath. Most manuscripts, among them early papyri and Codex Vaticanus, have the words; some add "only". A footnote gives the shorter reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: bathed: washed the whole body; wash: wash a part of the body
decisions.reason: Jesus uses two different verbs. The first is for bathing the whole body; the second, used throughout this passage for the feet, is for washing a part. A guest who had bathed at home needed only to wash the dust from the feet on arrival.

decisions.choice: clean: made clean by Jesus and belonging to him; the bath is a cleansing that need not be repeated
alternatives: the foot-washing is a further, repeated cleansing from daily wrongs for those already clean
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the picture of the bath to speak of a cleansing the disciples have already received. In 15:3 he says that they are clean because of the word he has spoken to them. The foot-washing may stand for that same cleansing given through his death, or for a further cleansing that those already clean still need. The text does not settle which. A footnote gives the second view.

decisions.choice: you are clean: Jesus turns from Peter to all the disciples, with one exception
decisions.reason: "You" is now plural. "Not all" points to Judas, as the narrator explains in verse 11. Judas has had his feet washed with the rest, but he is not clean.

decisions.choice: bathed / taken a bath; wash
decisions.reason: Every level keeps two different English verbs for the two Greek verbs (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: clean all over first, then the feet
decisions.reason: Readable puts the main point first in short sentences: the bathed person is clean, and only the feet need washing.

decisions.choice: bañarse; lavarse
decisions.reason: Two verbs, as in Greek: a bath of the whole body, and washing a part (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros
decisions.reason: Jesus turns from Peter to all the disciples (meaning decision m4), so the plural takes the setting.

decisions.choice: kuoga (bathe); kuosha (wash)
decisions.reason: Two verbs, as in the Greek and the English: "kuoga" is washing the whole body, "kuosha" washing a part of it. "Kutawadha" is the ritual washing before prayer and would bring in a practice the verse does not mean.

decisions.choice: "tắm" (bathe) and "rửa" (wash)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese has the same distinction as the Greek between washing the whole body and washing a part, so the two verbs are kept apart.

source.text: ᾔδει γὰρ τὸν παραδιδόντα αὐτόν· διὰ τοῦτο εἶπεν ὅτι Οὐχὶ πάντες καθαροί ἐστε.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knew the one handing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over; because of this {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Not all of you are clean."
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knew who was going to betray {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; this is the reason {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Not all of you are clean."
en.R: Jesus knew who was going to betray {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Not all of you are clean."

es.L: Porque sabía quién lo entregaba; por eso dijo: «No todos {{plural_you:están|estáis}} limpios».
es.B: Porque sabía quién lo iba a traicionar; por esa razón dijo: «No todos {{plural_you:están|estáis}} limpios».
es.R: Jesús sabía quién lo iba a traicionar. Por eso dijo: «No todos {{plural_you:están|estáis}} limpios».

sw.L: Kwa maana alimfahamu yule anayemtoa; kwa sababu hiyo alisema, "Si wote kati yenu walio safi."
sw.B: Kwa maana alijua ni nani atakayemsaliti; hiyo ndiyo sababu alisema, "Si wote kati yenu walio safi."
sw.R: Yesu alijua ni nani atakayemsaliti. Kwa hiyo akasema, "Si wote kati yenu walio safi."

vi.L: Vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} biết người sẽ nộp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; vì thế {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phán: "Không phải tất cả các con đều sạch."
vi.B: Vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} biết ai sẽ phản bội {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; đó là lý do {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phán: "Không phải tất cả các con đều sạch."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu biết ai sẽ phản bội {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Vì vậy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Không phải tất cả các con đều sạch."

decisions.choice: for: the narrator explains Jesus's words to the reader
decisions.reason: John steps in to explain "not all" (13:10). He does not say that the disciples understood it; in 13:28-29 they still do not know what Judas is about to do.

decisions.choice: the one handing him over: the betrayer, whose betrayal is already under way
decisions.reason: The participle is present: the betrayal is already set in motion (13:2), though not yet done. It can also be taken as "the one who would hand him over"; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: Jesus knew: he was not taken by surprise
decisions.reason: John has said from early on that Jesus knew who would betray him (6:64, 70-71), and Jesus will say so again (13:18-19). He washes Judas's feet with full knowledge.

decisions.choice: handing him over (L); was going to betray (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 13:2 and 6:71 (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Jesus; So
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus and joins the two sentences with "So" for the Greek "because of this".

decisions.choice: lo entregaba (L); lo iba a traicionar (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "nộp" (L); "phản bội" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "hand over" as "nộp"; Balanced and Readable say plainly what it was, as the English does.
